2027-06-14.title: Fifth Monday of the Apostles
2027-06-14.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Suffering was to make us rely on God
2027-06-14.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), which began at Pentecost: the Church remembers how the apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, carried the Gospel to the nations. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and from Pentecost the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. The Syro-Malankara calendar remembers the prophet Elisha today.
2027-06-14.verse: I have said this to you, so that in me you may have peace. In the world you face persecution. But take courage; I have conquered the world!”
theo: The Gospel takes us back to the Upper Room on the night before the Passion. Jesus has spoken at length to his disciples, and now he says, “I have said these things to you in figures of speech. The hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures, but will tell you plainly of the Father.” He promises a new closeness in prayer: “On that day you will ask in my name. I do not say to you that I will ask the Father on your behalf; for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God.” Jesus does not stand between us and a distant, reluctant Father, persuading him to be kind; he brings us into the Father's own love. Then he sums up his whole mission in one sentence: “I came from the Father and have come into the world; again, I am leaving the world and am going to the Father.” The disciples are delighted: “Yes, now you are speaking plainly… by this we believe that you came from God.” But Jesus knows how fragile their certainty is: “Do you now believe? The hour is coming, indeed it has come, when you will be scattered, each one to his home, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone because the Father is with me.” Within hours they would run from Gethsemane. And yet his last word that night is not a reproach but a promise: “I have said this to you, so that in me you may have peace. In the world you face persecution. But take courage; I have conquered the world!” He announces the victory before the battle, on the eve of the Cross. In this Season of the Apostles we know how the story continued: the men who scattered that night were gathered again by the risen Lord, filled with the Spirit at Pentecost, and sent to the ends of the earth, where they did not run away again.

Paul's letter shows us one of those apostles in the thick of the world's persecution, and he is honest about it: “We do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, of the affliction we experienced in Asia; for we were so utterly, unbearably crushed that we despaired of life itself.” We do not know exactly what happened in the Roman province of Asia, whether it was the riot at Ephesus (Acts 19), an imprisonment or a severe illness. What we do know is that a great apostle reached the point where he could not go on. Holiness does not mean having no breaking point. Paul tells us what he learned there: “Indeed, we felt that we had received the sentence of death so that we would rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead.” The faith of Easter is not only for the end of life; it is for the hospital corridor, the failed examination, the business that collapsed, the marriage that seems dead. The God who raised Jesus from the tomb can raise us from what crushes us. Paul's hope then stretches across time: “He who rescued us from so deadly a peril will continue to rescue us; on him we have set our hope that he will rescue us again.” Past rescue becomes the ground of future trust.

Then Paul adds something that every parish should hear: “as you also join in helping us by your prayers, so that many will give thanks on our behalf for the blessing granted us through the prayers of many.” The apostle who founded Churches asks the Churches to carry him in prayer. Prayer for one another is not a pious extra; it is real help, and when God answers, the thanksgiving too becomes common. So Jesus was not alone, because the Father was with him; and Paul was not alone, because the Church was praying. Neither are we. Our evening family prayer, the intentions of the family unit, the names read out in the parish, the Karozutha of the Holy Qurbana in which the deacon lifts up the sick and the suffering: all these are the prayers of many through which God keeps rescuing his people. Whoever is crushed today should be able to say, with Paul, I am not carrying this alone.
outline: Ask: when was I last crushed beyond my strength, and who prayed for me?
Point 1 · Crushed, so as to rely on God
Paul's affliction in Asia; the God who raises the dead.
Helping one another by prayer; thanksgiving made in common.
Point 3 · Take courage, I have conquered the world
The scattered disciples, the Father who is with Jesus, peace in him.
live: Rely on God who raises the dead (2 Corinthians 1:9)
Name the thing that crushes you most right now and pray each day this week: Lord, raise me up from this.
Write down the names of three people who are suffering and pray for them each evening at family prayer this week; send one of them a message that you are praying.
fathers: The Father loves you, Jesus says, because you have loved me. But did we love first? No: he loved us so that we might love him. Our love for Christ is itself the Father's gift, and when he crowns our love he crowns his own gifts.

See how Paul, great as he was, asks the prayers of the faithful. He teaches us that the prayers of many, even of the lowly, obtain great things from God; and he wants the thanksgiving to be made by many too, so that the favour given to one becomes a feast of praise for all.
magis: Faith in God the Father almighty can be put to the test by the experience of evil and suffering; but God revealed his almighty power in the most mysterious way in the voluntary humiliation and the Resurrection of his Son, by which he conquered evil.
Intercession is a prayer of petition which leads us to pray as Jesus did; in the time of the Church, Christian intercession participates in Christ's, as an expression of the communion of saints.
Suffering, a consequence of original sin, acquires a new meaning when it is united to the saving Passion of Jesus; it becomes a participation in his saving work.
saints: No saint's memorial is kept in the Syro-Malabar or the Latin calendar today. The Syro-Malankara calendar remembers the prophet Elisha, the disciple of Elijah who received a double share of his spirit.

13–18 June: the fifth week of the Season of the Apostles. Sun 13: Fifth Sunday of the Apostles (in the Latin calendar the memorial of St Antony of Padua gives way to the Sunday). Wed 16: in the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu) begins. Sat 19: Sts Gervasius and Protasius are listed in the calendar. Sun 20: Sixth Sunday of the Apostles. Ahead: Thu 24 June, the Birth of John the Baptist; Tue 29 June, Sts Peter and Paul, a day of obligation.
2027-06-14.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, on the night before you suffered you told your disciples that they would scatter and leave you alone, and still you promised them peace. Father, you were with your Son in his loneliness, and you raised him from the dead. When we are crushed beyond our strength, teach us to rely not on ourselves but on you, who raise the dead. Make us a people who carry one another in prayer, and who give thanks together for every rescue. Take courage in us, Lord, for you have conquered the world. To the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit be glory for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we celebrate the victory that Jesus announced on the eve of his Passion. The Body that was broken and the Blood that was poured out are the proof that he has conquered the world.
The whole Church prays here together, the living and the saints, so that whoever comes crushed may go out in peace.

quick: Paul: we were so crushed that we despaired of life, so that we would rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead.
Paul: help us by your prayers, so that many may give thanks for the blessing granted through the prayers of many.
Jesus: you will be scattered and leave me alone, yet I am not alone; take courage, I have conquered the world.
2027-06-14.action: Pray each evening this week for three people who are suffering, and tell one of them you are praying.
2027-06-14.question: What am I trying to carry on my own strength?

family.explain: Saint Paul once had such a hard time that he felt he could not go on. But he trusted God, and he asked his friends to pray for him. When God helped him, everyone thanked God together. Jesus also told his friends that they would have troubles in the world, but he said, “Take courage; I have conquered the world!” When someone in our family or our class is going through a hard time, we can help them by praying for them.
family.intention: We pray for people who are very sick, very sad, or in danger, especially those we know by name.
family.ask: Ask: “Who needs our prayers this week? Let us say their names together.”

illus: A father of three from a parish near Thrissur was brought to hospital after a road accident during the monsoon, and for four days the doctors could not say whether he would live. His wife sat outside the intensive care unit, too exhausted even to pray. On the second night her phone kept lighting up: the family unit had started a chain of prayer, each household taking an hour through the night; the Sunday school children were saying a decade of the rosary at the start of each class; the sisters in the nearby convent had placed his name before the Blessed Sacrament. ‘I could not pray,’ she said later, ‘so the parish prayed for me.’ He recovered slowly. On the Sunday he came back to church, walking with a stick, the vicar read out a simple notice of thanksgiving, and the whole church said ‘Thanks be to God’ together. That is what Saint Paul means by the prayers of many.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you have conquered the world and you give us your peace. We come to you with our burdens and with the burdens of others. Send your Holy Spirit to teach us to pray for one another. Amen.
share: We despaired of life itself (2 Corinthians 1:8). When have I reached my breaking point, and what did God do?
So that we would rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead (2 Corinthians 1:9). What am I still trying to carry alone?
Through the prayers of many (2 Corinthians 1:11). Who has carried me in prayer, and whom am I carrying?
Take courage; I have conquered the world (John 16:33). Where do I most need the peace of Jesus today?
pm.resp: Lord, raise us up and give us your peace.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may proclaim the victory of Christ with courage.
For Christians who are persecuted for their faith, that they may take courage in the Lord.
For the sick in hospitals, especially those in intensive care, and for their families waiting outside.
For those who are crushed by debt, failure or depression, that they may rely on God who raises the dead.
For our family units and prayer groups, that they may be true networks of prayer and thanksgiving.
pm.close: Father, your Son was never alone, because you were with him; you rescued your apostle Paul and you rescue us still. Teach us to rely on you, to carry one another in prayer, and to give you thanks together. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Saint Paul tells the Corinthians something surprising: “we were so utterly, unbearably crushed that we despaired of life itself” (2 Corinthians 1:8). The great apostle had a breaking point. If you feel today that you cannot go on, you are in good company.

Paul tells us why God allowed it: “so that we would rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead” (2 Corinthians 1:9). When our strength runs out, God's strength begins. The God who raised Jesus from the tomb can raise us from what crushes us.

And Paul asks for help: “join in helping us by your prayers.” Prayer for one another is real help. When we pray for the sick, the anxious, the poor, we carry them. And when God answers, we all give thanks together.

In the Gospel, Jesus tells his disciples that they will run away and leave him alone. “Yet I am not alone because the Father is with me.” Then he says: “In the world you face persecution. But take courage; I have conquered the world!” (John 16:32–33). He said this the night before he died. The victory was certain even before the battle.

So let us not carry our burdens alone. Let us bring them to the Lord who has conquered the world, and let us carry one another in prayer. Then many will give thanks for the blessings granted through the prayers of many. Amen.
kids: Children, sometimes even big people feel that their problems are too heavy. Saint Paul felt like that. But he trusted God, and his friends prayed for him. When you are sad or scared, tell Jesus, and ask your family to pray with you. And when a friend is sad, pray for them! Jesus says: “Take courage; I have conquered the world!”

An apostle crushed beyond his strength, the prayers of many that carry him, and the Lord who is never alone and has conquered the world.

points.apply: Name what crushes you most and pray daily this week for God to raise you up from it.

sub: Scattered disciples, a Lord never alone.
Victory announced on the eve of the Cross.
q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
I have said this to you, so that in me you may have peace. In the world you face persecution. But take courage; I have conquered the world!”
points.apply: Bring your heaviest burden to the next Holy Qurbana and leave it with the Lord who has conquered the world.

concl: God allows us to reach the end of our strength so that we may rely on him who raises the dead.
We are never alone: the Father is with the Son, the Church carries us in prayer, and Christ has conquered the world.
2027-06-14.resolve: This week, pray daily for God to raise you up from what crushes you, carry three suffering people in prayer, and take courage in Christ's victory.
